hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to repeating arrays of high-contrast, parallel vertical lines or bars, effectively forming a visual grating pattern. These features typically manifest as structural slats, tubes, fins, or slots—such as those found on cribs, radiators, organ pipes, xylophone resonators, and car grilles—or as organic striping patterns like those on a zebra. The activating pattern is characterized by a strict alternation between light and dark bands; most commonly, the feature consists of light-colored vertical elements (white, cream, silver, gold, or light wood) separated by deep shadows or dark gaps (black, dark brown, or dark grey), though the inverse (dark stripes on light) is also effective. The neuron is invariant to the specific object identity, material properties, and lighting conditions, provided the periodicity and high contrast of the vertical structures are maintained. The repeating pattern typically dominates the composition, occupying approximately 50–90% of the image area and extending across the majority of the frame's width or height.

Centered in the view is the front fascia of a silver Jeep Wrangler, captured directly head-on under bright daylight conditions. The dominant feature is the iconic grille, composed of seven vertical, pill-shaped slots with black mesh interiors, set against the metallic silver body panel. A white wooden crib dominates the central view, viewed from a slightly elevated angle looking down into the enclosure through a foreground of vertical slats. Inside, against a backdrop of more white vertical slats on the far side, sit two plush toys resting on a mattress. To the left, a golden-yellow teddy bear sits upright, facing slightly toward the right; it features a lighter cream-colored muzzle, a distinct black nose, and beady dark eyes, wearing a small garment patterned with blue and green tones. The foreground horizontal top rail of the crib cuts across the lower middle portion of the visible area, framing the scene.

Viewing the object from a slightly elevated, angled perspective, the lower half of the visible area is dominated by a series of vertical, cylindrical resonator tubes finished in a matte metallic gold. These tubes are arranged in a dense row, graduating in length from long on the left, where the bottom edge is cut off, to significantly shorter on the right, where they end well above the bottom of the frame. Each visible tube is capped at the bottom with a black circular plug. Above these resonators lies the instrument's keyboard, composed of smooth, rectangular wooden bars in a deep reddish-brown hue with visible wood grain. The bars are arranged in two parallel rows; the front row, corresponding to natural notes, overlays the front resonators, while a second row for accidental notes is set slightly further back and elevated, positioned above a rear set of partially visible gold tubes. The bars are suspended by thin cords running horizontally through their nodal points. Supporting the keyboard is a thick wooden frame rail, matching the color of the bars, which runs horizontally across the middle of the view. A black metal hinge plate, secured with six silver rivets arranged in two columns of three, connects a joint in the wooden rail slightly to the right of the center. Hanging on the far right edge of the frame is a black fabric bag, partially obscuring the rightmost tubes; tucked inside one of its pockets are two percussion mallets with thin, pale wooden shafts and bright magenta spherical heads. The entire apparatus stands on a plain, light gray floor, which occupies the bottom right quadrant of the view, featuring soft, diffuse shadows cast directly beneath the resonator tubes.

A close-up, slightly high-angle view captures a section of a stainless steel kitchen appliance, dominated by metallic silver and gray tones with high-contrast reflections. At the top, four evenly spaced, diagonal slots recede into the machine, revealing dark interiors containing textured, coil-like wire heating elements. Below these intake-like openings runs a prominent, horizontal cylindrical bar of polished stainless steel, which catches a bright, linear specular highlight along its length, indicating an overhead light source. Beneath this bar lies a flat vertical panel featuring a row of approximately fifteen narrow, vertical, capsule-shaped ventilation slots, uniformly spaced and dark against the bright metal. Below this upper vent row is a smooth, unadorned section of the steel panel, centered around a vertical control mechanism. This mechanism consists of a black, vertical slot housing a lever with a small, round, black knob at its top and a cylindrical shaft extending downward. To the right of this lever, a second, lower row of vertical ventilation slots begins, identical in width but slightly shorter than the upper row, continuing towards the right edge. On the far right edge, partially obscured, is a curved section of a large black dial or knob. The metal surface throughout exhibits subtle horizontal brushing and varying gradients of light and shadow, reinforcing the metallic texture.

A series of vertical, cylindrical metal tubes, resembling polished aluminum or silver, dominates the composition, hanging in a densely packed row that spans the width of the view. These tubes are suspended from a thick, horizontal wooden bar made of light-colored, smooth-grained timber that runs across the upper portion of the scene. The metal cylinders are arranged in graduated lengths, with the longest tubes positioned on the left side, reaching almost to the bottom, and progressively shortening in length towards the right side. The surfaces of the tubes are highly reflective, displaying vertical streaks of bright white highlights and varying shades of grey that emphasize their roundness and metallic texture. On the left side, behind the primary row of tubes, partial glimpses of a second, rear row of similar cylinders are visible. A distinct anomaly occurs at the bottom of the second tube from the left in the front row; instead of ending straight down, it features a mitred joint where a short section of tubing angles sharply to the right at approximately 45 degrees, terminating in a flat, circular cap that visually overlaps the bottom of the third tube. Behind the array of tubes, particularly visible on the right side, is a second horizontal wooden structural element, matching the tone of the top bar, which runs behind the tubes. Below this secondary wooden bar and behind the shorter tubes is a dark, matte charcoal-grey rectangular panel. At the very bottom of the image, a section of light wood flooring with vertical grain is visible, providing a base beneath the suspended apparatus. The lighting is distinct, creating strong specular reflections on the convex metal surfaces and casting soft, diffuse shadows on the wooden components and the floor below.

Viewed from a high angle, a section of a tuned percussion instrument spans diagonally across the frame from the upper left to the lower right against a pitch-black background. Two parallel rows of rectangular wooden bars, colored in varying shades of warm amber and medium brown with visible linear grain, are suspended by a thin white cord that threads horizontally through the nodal points of each bar. The lower row of bars, positioned closer to the foreground, forms a continuous sequence of approximately thirteen visible slats, while the upper row, set slightly further back and elevated, is arranged in clusters of two and three separated by gaps, mirroring a piano's accidental key layout. Separating these two rows is a structural rail painted a solid, reddish-brown earth tone. Beneath each wooden bar hangs a corresponding tubular resonator; these cylinders are a pale, creamy yellow, appearing almost white where the light hits them most directly. The resonators are arranged vertically but appear angled toward the bottom left due to the instrument's overall diagonal tilt, forming a dense, fence-like array that descends into the darkness below. Strong lighting creates bright, longitudinal highlights along the left curvature of the resonator tubes, contrasting sharply with the deep shadows between them. The bars and tubes taper slightly in size from left to right, indicating a progression in pitch, with the tops of the bars reflecting a soft, satin sheen.

A dense array of approximately twenty vertical metal organ pipes dominates the upper two-thirds of the view, arranged side-by-side within a warm-toned wooden cabinet. The pipes are cylindrical and metallic, transitioning in color from a cool, reflective silver-grey on the left to an intense, glowing yellow-gold on the right due to a strong, warm light source emanating from the right side. Each pipe features a distinct mouth—a horizontal slit with a flattened upper lip and a tapered foot below—located roughly one-third of the way up from the bottom of the metal section. These mouths form a gentle, upward-curving line across the width of the array. The tops of the pipes are arranged in a shallow arch, with the central pipes being slightly shorter than those flanking them, though the upper tips are largely obscured. Vertical highlights streak the length of the pipes, accentuating their rounded curvature. Below the row of pipes is a polished wooden structure in shades of medium honey-brown. A horizontal wooden rail supports the base of the pipes. Just below the center of this rail, a single, cylindrical white stop or knob protrudes outward, catching the light on its upper surface. Beneath this knob is a rectangular panel featuring a darker, reddish-brown horizontal band sandwiched between lighter wood tones. On the lower left edge of the wooden casing, a vertical column of three small white circular buttons or studs is visible, while a similar but less distinct arrangement appears on the lower right edge, partially obscured by shadow. The background behind the upper pipes is dark and indistinct, providing high contrast to the illuminated metal flutes.

A vintage-style illustration of an accordion dominates the view, rendered in dark, chocolate-brown ink against a textured, creamy beige background. The central focus is the instrument's bellows, which extend fan-like from the left center toward the right edge, comprised of approximately sixteen visible vertical folds. These pleats are defined by thick, shadowed lines in the valleys and lighter, stippled textures on the protruding ridges, creating a sense of depth and volume. To the left of the bellows, the accordion's treble housing is visible, featuring a dark, solid vertical strip reinforced at the top corner with a decorative, triangular metal bracket held in place by three distinct, circular rivets. Further left, along the curved edge of the casing, a vertical column of four oval-shaped buttons is partially visible, depicted in white against a dark, heavily shaded background. The side of the casing below the metal bracket shows horizontal hatching lines, suggesting a textured grille or strap mechanism. Hovering in the upper region of the cream background, disconnected from the main instrument, are two small, fragmentary drawing elements: to the upper left, a curved, segmented piece resembling a detached strap or handle with cross-hatching, and to the upper right, a rectangular fragment depicting a small section of white and black piano keys or a similar horizontally lined structure. The entire composition uses a woodcut or engraving aesthetic, relying on high contrast between the dense, dark linework and the pale paper tone to define distinct geometric forms and mechanical details.

Dominating the upper two-thirds of the scene is a massive, multi-story hotel facade that curves gently outward in its central section, illuminated by a cool, violet-blue artificial wash. The building features a rigorous, repetitive grid of dark rectangular windows separated by light-colored vertical piers and horizontal bands, creating a dense, textured surface. Scattered sparsely across the dark grid are a few windows emitting a warm, orange glow, contrasting with the prevailing cool tones. The top of the structure is capped with a decorative cornice line featuring vertical accents, lit with a warmer, yellowish hue. Occupying the lower third of the view is a dramatic display of illuminated water fountains shooting upward in the foreground. A series of powerful vertical jets form a jagged wall of bright white water, varying slightly in height, while beneath them, intersecting arcs of water spray in parabolic curves, creating a lattice-like pattern near the base. The water is brilliantly lit from below, appearing as a stark white and cream mist against the darker, shadowed base and the purple building behind it, with the spray blurring into a soft texture where the streams dissipate. The fountains are positioned directly in front of the architecture, obscuring the ground level and lower floors of the building, creating a layered depth between the bright, fluid foreground and the rigid, geometric background.

The central subject is the midsection and flank of a zebra lying horizontally on its side, occupying the majority of the view against a background of dry, pebbly earth. The zebra's coat features a high-contrast pattern of deep charcoal-black stripes against a creamy off-white background. On the main torso, these stripes run vertically and are roughly parallel, slightly curving around the barrel of the body; as they descend toward the belly, the black lines narrow and eventually terminate, leaving the lowermost underbelly distinctively white and unpatterned. To the left, near the shoulder region, the striping pattern shifts diagonally, forming a chevron-like convergence where the neck meets the body, while on the far right, the stripes over the hip curve horizontally to follow the contour of the haunch. A rear leg is tucked beneath the body at the bottom right, displaying dense horizontal banding that extends down to a light beige-grey hoof resting on the ground. A portion of a front leg and hoof is partially visible on the bottom left, positioned beneath the chest area. The animal's back forms a gentle, concave curve along the top edge of the subject, above which lies a patch of ground composed of light brown dirt scattered with small, irregular grey stones and gravel. The lighting is soft and diffuse from above, highlighting the upper curvature of the zebra's ribs and back, while casting a soft, dark shadow underneath the belly where the body meets the darker, shadowed soil.

A pale, honey-colored wooden crib dominates the central visual field, angled so that its front corner faces the left and its long side extends toward the right. The crib is constructed from smooth, satin-finished natural wood, characterized by a series of evenly spaced, flat vertical slats with rounded edges that form the enclosure. Behind these wooden bars, a crisp white fabric bumper lines the interior, creating a solid white background between the slats. Along the gently curved upper rail of the long side, four large, pristine white ribbon bows are tied at regular intervals; one bow sits directly at the angled corner join on the left, while three others are distributed to the right, their loops flopping softly and tails hanging down against the wood. A horizontal wooden rail runs along the bottom of the slats, and near the right edge of this rail, small, dark, capitalized text is printed on the surface. Rising from the rear structure, a slender vertical wooden pole supports a canopy element, with translucent, gauzy white fabric draping vertically down the far right edge of the scene. The background features vertical tongue-and-groove wooden paneling in a slightly warmer, pinkish-beige tone compared to the crib, illuminated by soft, diffused lighting that creates gentle shadows beneath the furniture and highlights the sheen on the ribbon fabric.
